tagline: Over the mountains to a ranch the mail mules once served.
intro: Twenty-three miles down the Merlin-Galice Road, across the Graves Creek Bridge, Mt. Reuben Road turns off and climbs along the rugged edges of the Rogue River canyon. It winds on through the Siskiyou Mountains and ends, about 33 miles from the start, at the Rogue River Ranch at Marial.

Down on the water the Rogue River Trail runs between the same two points on foot, 24 miles from Grave Creek to Marial, on a path the Takelma made first and miners and settlers improved as they pushed deeper into the canyon.

moments.title: Rainie Falls Overlook
moments.text: High above the class V rapid of the same name, the overlook faces a 13-foot hexagonal abutment, one of the few remnants of a 1908 suspension bridge the 1927 flood took out.

moments.title: Rogue River Ranch
moments.text: Marial, named for a Billings daughter, kept its post office until 1954, by then the last in the country served only by mule pack trains.

practical: Beyond the Galice-Hellgate byway the country is remote with no services, so the BLM advises a full tank, a first aid kit, food and water, and roads out here are often closed by snow in winter.

sources.label: FHWA, Grave Creek to Marial Back Country Byway
